description: sessiontools' hooks, installed with the plugin. PostToolBatch: settle-hook, the settle alert. Once per model turn that calls a tool, it says ONE line once this session's context is at or past the threshold it set for itself, and nothing otherwise. SESSION_SETTLE_AT sets the threshold in tokens (250000, 250k, 1.5M); UNSET IS SILENT, ALWAYS, and python never starts. SESSION_SETTLE_SAY replaces the line ({at} and {used} are filled). SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_SETTLE=off (or 0/false/no) switches it off with the plugin still loaded. No filter on who the session is: any session with a threshold is told. A subagent's batch (payload agent_id) is silent. It reads the count with sessiontools.window.scan on the payload's transcript once this batch's own assistant row is there: the hook can start before that row is written, so when the payload names its tool calls it waits for the row, at most 1 s, then counts what is on disk. Otherwise it never blocks, and fails SILENT: no python3, python older than 3.11, a missing transcript or a crash all exit 0 with no output (hooks/settle-hook). PostToolBatch: clock-hook, the clock line, OFF BY DEFAULT: with SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_CLOCK=on (or 1/true/yes) in the environment it says on every batch the time and this session's context as used/max (`[clock] 12:34 UTC | ctx 182K/1.00M (18%)`; `ctx 182K/?` when the window is unknown, `ctx ?` with no reading), plus a second line once the count reaches SESSION_CLOCK_WARN_AT (tokens like 250k, or a percent of the window like 80%; unset is no warn line), with no mail count, the same batch-row wait and count as settle-hook, a subagent's batch silent, off exiting 0 before python starts, and any failure exiting 0 with no output (hooks/clock-hook, sessiontools.clockline). PreToolUse, PostToolBatch, Stop (verb stop), UserPromptSubmit, SessionEnd: busy-sound, the busy sound. It plays a sound file once a tool batch has run past a delay, and stops it the moment the batch returns. SILENT UNLESS SET: the `sounds` settings (~/.sessionkit/tools/settings/sounds.json, agent front matter, seats/<seat>/settings/, sessions/<sid>/settings/) need enabled: true and busy.{auto_arm: true, file, delay}. A seat without them starts python once per session (at its first tool; at its first Stop when that comes first), then pays a few stat calls per tool and per Stop. busy.trigger picks ONE mode: batch (unset; these hooks), landed or finished (signalled, not hooked: `session sound landed|given` plays and stops landed on sounds/unread; finished is held); any other value is silent in every mode, and a seat whose trigger is not batch is OFF for these hooks, paying what a seat without the setting pays. SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_BUSY=off (or 0/false/no) switches it off with the plugin still loaded. A subagent's batch makes no sound. The player is afplay, in a detached process group that the batch end kills; end and clear stop every slot (busy, unread, finished). busy.player picks who plays the batch trigger's sound: afplay (unset) or engine, the resident sound engine. With engine, the session's first arm starts python once to write the engine's record (sounds/busy/engine.<claude pid>) and send arm; every later hook sends ONE OSC datagram (/sound/event ,ssd EVENT SID T) to UDP 127.0.0.1:44100 with the native sender (~/.local/share/sessiontools/sound/bin/sound-event, or under SESSIONTOOLS_SOUND_HOME), with no python and no wait (a Stop still starts python when a stop sound is set). Not installed, or an engine that is off, is silent; any other player value is silent in every mode. Stop (verb stop) also plays the STOP SOUND, after it clears the slots: with enabled: true and stop.file set, it queues that file ONCE per Stop through the mouth's queue (mouth play FILE, so it lands after any line still speaking), and plays it with afplay only when the mouth is absent, exits non-zero or cannot be run; a mouth that times out or is killed by a signal is not followed by afplay, so it never plays twice. The play runs in a detached process group, so the hook never waits for it, and no clear cuts it: it is not a slot. Unset, a bad value or a subagent's Stop is silent. An OFF stamp, sounds/stop/off, back-dated and invalidated by a newer host- or session-layer sounds file as sounds/busy/off is, keeps a seat without it from starting python at Stop; the first arm writes it too. It never blocks, and fails SILENT (hooks/busy-sound, sessiontools.busy). The same busy-sound hooks keep the TURN-ENDED MARK, so a seat whose turn is over while a background agent runs reads `idle with children`, not busy. DEFAULT OFF: nothing is written unless SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_TURN=on (or 1/true/yes) is in the seat's environment; switching it on is a config change. On: Stop writes ~/.session/sessions/<sid>/turn-ended (under SESSIONS_DIR when set; only when the session dir exists) atomically, one JSON line {"v": 1, "at": <epoch s>, "harness": "claude-code", "event": "Stop", "background": <running background_tasks, or null>}; PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit and SessionEnd unlink it. An event whose payload carries agent_id (a subagent's) changes nothing. The mark runs before every sound switch and fast path, costs one stat on PreToolUse when there is no mark, never blocks, and fails SILENT (hooks/busy-sound, sessiontools.turn). SessionStart (verbs title, context): session-info, the session-info hooks. DEFAULT OFF, each on its own switch, checked before python starts. SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_TITLE=on (or 1/true/yes): title sets the session title to the first 8 characters of the session id, on startup, resume and fork (or no source); never on clear or compact, where Claude Code does not apply a title, and never over a title the session already has (payload session_title, from --name, /rename or another hook). Because the title counts as a custom title, a bare /clear keeps it: the new session shows the previous short id, and a later resume keeps that title too. If a fork inherits its parent's title, the fork shows the parent's short id the same way; that is the harness's behaviour, not measured here. SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_SESSION_INFO=on (or 1/true/yes): context injects a short Session Info block, one line each for the session id, working directory, source and transcript path, on every source; an absent or empty value is left out, and a block left with no line is not emitted. On startup (or no source) the Session ID line is left out when SESSIONTOOLS_LAUNCH_INFO equals the session id: session start exports it when the launch-info it injected carries that id. On every other source the line is printed. A subagent's payload (agent_id) is silent. It never blocks, and fails SILENT: no python3, python older than 3.11, bad JSON or a crash all exit 0 with no output (hooks/session-info, sessiontools.session_info).
